subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Pakistani Chai Culture
description: A fast breakdown of Pakistani Chai Culture for builders.

hook.text: Pakistan is one of the world's largest tea importers despite growing almost none. Chai is its most consumed drink.

buildup.text: Pakistani chai is similar to Indian masala chai but often stronger, less spiced, and served in small glass cups.

discovery.text: Kashmiri pink tea (noon chai) is a specialty—made pink by baking soda reacting with green tea, then adding milk.

twist.text: Chai consumption in Pakistan has economic implications. The country spends over $600 million annually on tea imports.

climax.text: A former PM once asked Pakistanis to cut back to two cups daily to reduce imports. The public politely refused.

punchline.text: No tea farms, $600 million in imports. Pakistan loves what it cannot grow.

quiz.question: What makes Kashmiri noon chai pink?
options: Baking soda reacting with green tea, then adding milk
